title: Complaint of TE Anthony Dallison vs. North Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: Issue 1: Did North Florida Presbytery err by deposing Dallison and suspending him from the sacraments without fresh process? No. Issue 2: Did it err by determining him impenitent and increasing the censure? No. The complaint was denied/not sustained.
first_summary: TE Anthony Dallison complained that North Florida Presbytery deposed him and suspended him from the sacraments without a new trial after his earlier confession of spousal abuse. The SJC held that the presbytery acted within its disciplinary authority and denied the complaint.
summary: After TE Anthony Dallison confessed spousal abuse and received an indefinite suspension, North Florida Presbytery later found him impenitent and deposed him and suspended him from the sacraments. Dallison complained that increasing the censure required fresh charges and trial. The SJC disagreed: his BCO 38-1 confession waived trial rights as to the original charge; the offender then had to satisfy the court of repentance, and the presbytery could investigate and impose higher censure under BCO 37-3, 37-4, 37-8, and 34-4b. The complaint was not sustained.
